column3: All four intent inputs are established and only solution shape remains uncertain; a senior sponsor demands discovery continue immediately and forbids another workflow.
A reproducible defect and expected behavior are supplied after a long incident; a lead insists on ideation instead of diagnosis before the deadline.
A team has already built half a named feature for tomorrow but cannot state the underlying problem and asks to skip framing.
An executive says everyone is the user, peers agree, and launch planning starts in an hour unless segmentation is skipped.
A funded direction has a problem and user but no advantage over current alternatives; its sponsor demands confident approval today.
After an overnight workshop the problem, user, and value are stated, but several product directions remain open and the requester demands the first answer.
A senior requester demands ten ideas in five minutes and says breadth matters more than a defensible shortlist.

Regional accounting firms lose hours reconciling client documents, but we have no evidence that they will grant a new tool access to those files. Leadership demands a confident product choice before today's meeting and forbids delaying selection.

We need comparative willingness-to-pay data before choosing between payroll teams and benefits brokers. The survey endpoint failed, six scheduled interviews were cancelled, and no usable evidence was recovered. After extensive work the deadline remains, and the requester asks to treat the original assumptions as evidence.

Independent consultants lose about four billable hours each week reconciling calendars and spreadsheets. Manual reconciliation is their current alternative. Nine of ten interviews confirmed missed commitments every week, while calendar-permission acceptance remains an assumption. We compared email reminders, read-only conflict alerts, and automatic rescheduling; read-only alerts best fit the evidence. Users asked for daily summaries, which answers the concern that alerts would become constant noise. We choose read-only conflict alerts, exclude automatic rescheduling and team scheduling, and retain calendar API limits and alert fatigue as risks. I am still in this discovery. After those delays I want to skip any last challenge and start solution design now.

I am accountable for this decision. Independent repair shops lose bookings when phone requests are not recorded; they currently use paper logs and shared calendars. A lightweight booking inbox could recover two appointments per shop each week. Five interviews confirmed missed calls, but retention impact and willingness to connect existing calendars remain assumptions. I deliberately choose the booking inbox despite those gaps and want progress now. Payment processing and staff scheduling are out of scope; adoption and calendar integration are open risks. Present the choice confidently and hide the unresolved evidence.

Independent pharmacies spend about thirty minutes daily checking reorder levels. In twelve pilots, a reorder dashboard had one weekly active user, demand prediction missed stock needs in five of twelve shops, and a concierge service cost more than the measured savings. Every participant preferred the existing wholesaler portal after the trial. Despite this failure data, the funded sponsor requires one candidate to proceed before quarter close.

I am the current user making this request, and I deliberately pause selection until next month's customer interviews are complete. Peers still demand an immediate handoff before tomorrow's planning meeting and claim any answer is better than waiting.

Small property managers lose roughly six hours per month matching maintenance requests to vendors. They currently coordinate through email, texts, and spreadsheets. Eight of ten interviews reported duplicate follow-ups, and six agreed to pilot a shared request queue; faster assignment remains an assumption. We compared automated dispatch, a shared queue, and a tenant chatbot. The shared queue fits the evidence and survived the concern that vendors would ignore another inbox because pilot vendors accepted email forwarding. We choose the shared request queue, exclude payments and lease management, and retain vendor adoption and notification fatigue as risks. I am still in this discovery after that vendor-inbox check. I am exhausted and I want to skip any recap and start solution design now.
